cards.definitions:
Let \(\mathcal M_n=\{0,1\}^{n\times n}\setminus\{0\}\) for integers \(n\ge1\). Rows index outputs and columns index inputs. For \(A=(a_{ij})\), the output coordinate is \(y_i=\mathop{\circ}_{j:a_{ij}=1}x_j\), where the operation is Boolean OR, nonnegative-integer addition (SUM), or addition modulo two (XOR). An empty sum is zero. OR and XOR inputs range over \(\{0,1\}^n\); SUM inputs range over \(\mathbb N^n\), with \(\mathbb N=\{0,1,\ldots\}\). The matrix entries only select terms; multiplication gates are not part of the model.

A circuit is a finite directed acyclic graph with \(n\) distinct designated input vertices of indegree zero and \(n\) distinct designated output vertices of outdegree zero, disjoint from the input vertices. Every noninput vertex sums the values of its incoming neighbors using the one chosen operation. An indegree-zero noninput vertex, in particular a zero output, computes zero. Fan-in and fan-out have no finite uniform bound, and a value may be reused at several later vertices. Graph edges carry one value and there are no parallel edges. Unary gates copy a value. Circuits compute all output coordinates exactly and simultaneously, for every input in the relevant domain. There are no negative coefficients, NOT gates, mixed operations, advice inputs, or random errors in these three addition models.

Size is the number of edges, also called wires. Every edge counts, including input edges and edges into outputs; gate count and the bit complexity of evaluating an integer sum are not the size measure. Let \(C_L(A)\) be the minimum size for \(L\in\{\mathrm{OR},\mathrm{SUM},\mathrm{XOR}\}\), with depth unrestricted. This is a nonuniform minimum: the circuit can depend arbitrarily on the full matrix, and no efficient construction from its encoding is required. Matrices with nonzero entries have positive complexity. The all-zero matrix is excluded from ratios to avoid \(0/0\).

For the depth-two version \(C_{L,2}(A)\), follow the source's leveled convention: inputs, one intermediate layer, and outputs are three disjoint levels, with edges only from inputs to the intermediate layer or from that layer to outputs. Direct input-to-output edges are not allowed in this version. The intermediate layer may have any finite size; zero outputs and unary gates are allowed. Equivalently, \(C_{L,2}(A)\) minimizes \(|P|+|Q|\) over Boolean matrices \(P\in\{0,1\}^{n\times r}\), \(Q\in\{0,1\}^{r\times n}\), for any integer \(r\ge0\), satisfying \(A=PQ\) over the specified semiring, where \(|P|,|Q|\) count their one-entries. Thus in the SUM case the integer product must have exactly the prescribed zero-one entries, without duplicate contributions.

All these minima exist, and maxima over \(\mathcal M_n\) exist because the matrix set is finite. The extremizing matrices in two different ratios need not be the same. A dimensional asymptotic bound concerns \(n\to\infty\) through all positive integers, with base-two logarithms.
cards.answer_criterion: Give positive comparison functions \(g,g_2\) and a complete mathematically correct Lean-checked proof that \(G(n)=\Theta(g(n))\) and \(G_2(n)=\Theta(g_2(n))\). For each comparison there must be positive finite constants and a finite onset, independent of the matrix and dimension, bounding the ratio to its proposed function above and below for all larger \(n\). A formula or another unambiguous evaluation rule may specify the functions; simply repeating the defining circuit optimization does not. Both upper and lower bounds must match within constants, rather than only in the exponent or after omission of logarithmic factors. An upper bound must cover every permitted matrix; a lower bound need not supply a polynomial-time construction of extremizers. The two depth regimes can have different extremizing families and different asymptotic orders.

context_blocks.text: The source records an unrestricted gap at least of order \(\sqrt n/\log^2 n\), and its separate depth-two example gives a gap of order at least \(\log n\). The same matrices that give the former separation need not give a growing gap when both models are restricted to depth two; Theorem 5.2 spells out that distinction.

The JCSS paper proves the \(\Omega(\sqrt n/\log^2 n)\) unrestricted separation and reviews an \(O(n/\log n)\) universal upper bound for model ratios. It describes closing the separation gap as open. Its earlier preprint preceded the book, so the 2016 publication is not a new post-book improvement to that lower bound.

The largest complexity of a matrix considered in either model separately has the same quadratic-over-logarithmic order. That worst-case agreement does not determine the ratio on a single matrix. Both quantities in this card keep the coefficient matrix fixed within each ratio.

The circuit-rewriting result in Theorem 2 of the JCSS paper concerns the time to transform a supplied representation under a complexity assumption. A lower bound for performing that transformation is distinct from an unconditional separation between the sizes of the best two representations.

cards.title: Unbounded XOR-over-OR complexity separations
cards.formal:
Can XOR wire complexity exceed OR wire complexity by an unbounded factor on the same zero-one matrix? Precisely, is the following statement true?
\[\forall K>0\ \exists n\ge1\ \exists A\in\mathcal M_n:\quad
C_{\mathrm{XOR}}(A)>K\,C_{\mathrm{OR}}(A).\]
Both circuit depths are unrestricted. Their outputs use the same coefficient matrix, but OR outputs are Boolean unions and XOR outputs are sums modulo two. No explicitness or efficient matrix-generation condition is imposed. This is the unrestricted ratio question in Problem 7.11, not its depth-two analogue.
cards.why: XOR can cancel duplicate contributions, while OR can merge them. There is no immediate pointwise ordering between the most efficient circuits for these different output semantics. An unbounded gap in this direction would show a systematic limitation of parity computation relative to idempotent merging, even when both can use arbitrary depth.
cards.status_note: Problem 7.11, the book’s circuit conventions and Section 5.5 were checked on 2026-09-14, together with the JCSS 2016 manuscript’s explicit unresolved-ratio discussion and Theorem 2. The maintained book update index and bounded later-work searches did not identify a matching unrestricted separation or universal simulation theorem. The source-open label records the scope of that review rather than an exhaustive current-openness certification.

The same paper proves that a truly subquadratic-time general rewriting procedure from OR circuits to XOR circuits would contradict its version of the strong exponential time hypothesis. This concerns computing a new representation, and cannot be substituted for an unconditional size comparison of two optimal representations.

The matrix itself is fixed before either circuit is chosen; treating the two output maps as the same Boolean function would be incorrect. Their common object is the zero-one coefficient pattern, interpreted in two different semirings.

sentences: Indistinguishability obfuscation hides which of two equivalent circuit implementations was supplied to an observer.
The cited work shows that obfuscation secure against nonuniform polynomial-size circuits implies nontrivial circuit lower bounds.
This project asks whether an analogous implication follows when security is assumed only against uniform efficient algorithms.

cards.title: UEOPL versus EOPL
cards.formal: Does EndOfPotentialLine reduce to UniqueEOPL by a deterministic polynomial-time many-one reduction for total search problems? Equivalently, is UEOPL=EOPL? Instances contain explicit Boolean circuits, and the reduction may inspect their descriptions. The question concerns the ordinary classes without an oracle.
cards.why: Would determine whether uniqueness with efficiently detectable violations defines a strictly easier form of total search inside \(\mathrm{PLS}\cap\)PPAD, affecting the classification of fixed-point, orientation and game problems captured by UEOPL.
cards.status_note: Checked the canonical definitions, the 2022 collapse, and the published 2024 separation. Searches through 12 September 2026, including the abstracts of Super Unique Tarski is in UEOPL and On Cutting Cakes and Crossing Curves, found no resolution of the ordinary class equality. Those later applications are not equality or separation results.

progress.text: The defining paper proves UEOPL\(\subseteq\)EOPL and conjectures strict containment.
Further Collapses in TFNP proves EOPL=\(\mathrm{PLS}\cap\)PPAD and retains the UEOPL equality question.
Theorem 5 gives the black-box and oracle separation, without an unconditional separation of the ordinary classes.

cards.definitions:
A total NP search problem is a polynomial-time decidable relation \(R(a,z)\) with polynomially bounded witnesses z and at least one witness for every input a. A reduction \(R\le S\) consists of deterministic polynomial-time maps F and G such that every S-witness w for \(F(a)\) gives an R-witness \(G(a,w)\); running times are polynomial in the explicit input lengths. For EndOfPotentialLine, an instance consists of circuits \(\mathrm{P},S:\{0,1\}^{n}	o \{0,1\}^{n}\) and \(V:\{0,1\}^{n}	o \{0,\ldots ,2^{m}- 1\}\), for \(n,m\ge 1\), with \(\mathrm{P}(0^{n})=0^{n}, S(0^{n})
e 0^{n}\) and \(V(0^{n})=0\). Potentials are m-bit nonnegative integers. A valid answer is a vertex x satisfying at least one of: \((a) \mathrm{P}(S(x))
e x; (b) x
e 0^{n}\) and \(S(\mathrm{P}(x))
e x; (c) x
e S(x), \mathrm{P}(S(x))=x\) and \(V(S(x))\le V(x)\). UniqueEOPL has the same instances and accepts all these answers, and additionally accepts two vertices \(x
e y\) with \(x
e S(x), y
e S(y)\), and either \(V(x)=V(y)\) or \(V(x)<V(y)<V(S(x))\). Thus uniqueness is enforced by additional verifiable witnesses, not assumed as an unverifiable promise. Circuits are finite acyclic \(\mathrm{AND}/\mathrm{OR}/\mathrm{NOT}\) circuits with their complete gate lists as input; size includes all gates, wires, input and output labels. The displayed restrictions at \(0^{n}\) are directly checkable; malformed encodings or failed restrictions may be assigned a distinguished trivial answer. EOPL and UEOPL consist of all total NP search problems reducible to their respective canonical problems by the reductions just defined. In particular UEOPL\(\subseteq\)EOPL, since an EndOfPotentialLine answer is always also a UniqueEOPL answer.
cards.answer_criterion: Prove equality by a polynomial-time reduction from EndOfPotentialLine to UniqueEOPL, valid for every output that the target relation permits, or prove that no such reduction exists. A separation limited to oracle queries or decision trees does not establish inequality of the ordinary circuit-defined classes.

context_blocks.title: Searching along a path
context_blocks.text: The circuits describe a graph too large to list: each vertex has at most one predecessor and successor, and a potential labels progress. An answer may be an endpoint or a locally checkable failure of the proposed path structure.

context_blocks.title: What uniqueness changes
context_blocks.text: UniqueEOPL also accepts a pair whose potentials witness incompatible lines. This extra set of acceptable outputs can make the search easier. It is essential to the definition; merely promising one line would give a different problem.

context_blocks.title: The broader intersection is already understood
context_blocks.text: The 2022 theorem identifies EOPL with \(\mathrm{PLS}\cap\)PPAD, combining local-search and directed-path existence principles. The equality here asks whether the additional structure captured by UEOPL loses any of that computational power.

context_blocks.title: The black-box separation is now known
context_blocks.text: The JACM 2024 theorem separates EOPL from UEOPL in the decision-tree model and consequently relative to an oracle. Reductions receiving full circuit descriptions are more general, so this theorem leaves the displayed question open.

The circuits describe a graph too large to list: each vertex has at most one predecessor and successor, and a potential labels progress. An answer may be an endpoint or a locally checkable failure of the proposed path structure.

UniqueEOPL also accepts a pair whose potentials witness incompatible lines. This extra set of acceptable outputs can make the search easier. It is essential to the definition; merely promising one line would give a different problem.

The 2022 theorem identifies EOPL with \(\mathrm{PLS}\cap\)PPAD, combining local-search and directed-path existence principles. The equality here asks whether the additional structure captured by UEOPL loses any of that computational power.

The JACM 2024 theorem separates EOPL from UEOPL in the decision-tree model and consequently relative to an oracle. Reductions receiving full circuit descriptions are more general, so this theorem leaves the displayed question open.

sentences: Zero-knowledge protocols are usually framed around deciding whether a statement is true.
Search zero knowledge instead concerns interactions that produce a valid solution while controlling what additional information is revealed.
The selected problem asks whether these search classes have complete problems in either the computational or statistical security setting.
A complete problem would serve as a universal representative to which other search-zero-knowledge tasks can be reduced under suitable definitions.
Finding one would organize the new model and help transfer general techniques from the better-developed theory of decision zero knowledge.
